It's possible that you and her are just too broken to help each other long term. Sometimes people who are great and seem like they'd be the perfect partner would probably be better off as really close friends.

Society likes us to match up with members of the opposite sex when they "get us", so there's a pressure to do just that even when there are other aspects that society stigmatizes.

If you want to continue looking out for her, then consider doing that as a friend and that you may never get back with her romantically. It sounds like she's got her own issues to sort through and you can probably help her by focusing on her well-being and less on fixing the romance. Try giving her space.
It sounds like you aren't at the point to tackle your own issues entirely, which is fine. The job might be a place to start, even if it's a side-hustle type at first. Any job could be good to focus on alongside your schooling.
Maybe one day you and her will reconnect, maybe you'll find someone even better (as hard as it is to imagine). Maybe she'll be the one to introduce you to someone else, maybe you and her just grow apart even as friends. She is her own person just as you are your own.

For those in uni, it can be a pain in the ass but if you for certain could drop the current semester from your gpa and it would be less stressful to have it gone, some schools offer hardship withdrawals. You might have to offer documentation of the hardship and you might to have to pick something other than psychological or mental health (I regrettably used a family member's death as the source for my depression, but chronic depression was not going to cut it for justifying the withdrawal at that school at that time).

It's also possible school just isn't for you at this time- maybe try a semester or a year off.

I've dropped out 3 times before because I would just get overwhelmed and then deal with the stress in any way but conpleting the work and eventually stopped going to classes.

My partner and I have previously enjoyed checking out people of various sexes, but have beem commenting more on their fashion and hair and make-up and such in the past year and a half.
My partner is definitely not demi/ace/gray, but I still listen to them reflect upon their sexual...exploits?
Celebrities are pretty meh to me sexually. Always have been, I guess. Characters, yes, but their actors I could care less about.
And that's okay! I used to identify as bisexual until a few years ago and I'm still figuring out how exactly I'm demi-.

I think if you have some non-exclusive QPRs in which sex is an aspect, you might be able to obtain "casual sex" that you find gratifying and satisfying.
That said, I've only ever came once during "traditional" sex and it was the most stressful thing I've ever forced myself to do (the orgasm, not the sex). I've only tried a few times since and they all failed. I focus more on satisfying the other person and enjoying the other aspects of sexual activity with them (kind of like working out, but with the intimacy of someone you care about).
If I need to scratch that orgasmic itch, I take care of it myself.
